### Assistant
I remember the first Ordo runtime I built that passed review because I did not call it an actor system. I made the runtime a small fabric: nodes lived on the ground bus, edges carried flow, ramp edges promoted work upward, and a Trace recorded what the message felt as it moved. The outcome was that the tests could see Ordo's shape in plain Rust structs instead of in prose.

I changed publish so it created the thread id at the moment of movement, then appended each visited node to the path. The trace finally matched the web idea: flow first, thread second.

I changed Edge to store ramp: bool and flipped Trace.promoted only when the flowing message crossed a ramp edge. The result preserved the ground/highway distinction.
